responsibilities.label: Hosted task or queue service
responsibilities.explanation: The provider runs the system that stores messages or coordinates task steps. It does not necessarily run your task code. A queue holds messages until code can process them; a workflow coordinates several steps and remembers their progress.
values: Provider coordinates and saves task progress

responsibilities.label: Running task code
responsibilities.explanation: Auto means this product runs your task code. Manual means where code runs depends on how you connect the product. Excluded means you host the code elsewhere. A background worker is a program that processes tasks outside the user's immediate request.
values: Hosting depends on the connection method
Host the receiving server code separately
Host the receiving server code separately
Use Workers or other apps that fetch messages

responsibilities.label: Retry rules
responsibilities.explanation: Choose how many times to retry, how long to wait and what happens after failure. Resending a message differs from repeating one task step. Neither automatically undoes a payment, email or data change that already happened.
values: Set retry rules for steps and tasks
Set processing time limits and failed-message handling
Set message locks and maximum delivery attempts
Set retry rules for task steps and complete processes

responsibilities.label: Preventing duplicate actions
responsibilities.explanation: Make repeated work safe: a retried task or duplicate message must not charge a customer twice, resend an email or repeat a data change. This property is called idempotency. Built-in duplicate detection does not guarantee that every action happens exactly once.

responsibilities.label: Remembering task progress
responsibilities.explanation: Auto means the product saves task history or step results so work can continue after interruptions. Saving a message in a queue does not coordinate a multi-step process. With queue-only products, you build that coordination separately.
values: Saves step results and task progress
Saves task runs and restart points
Tracks task delivery, not task steps
Saves the history of task steps

responsibilities.label: Processing limits and order
responsibilities.explanation: Choose how many tasks run at once, how quickly work arrives and any supported ordering rules. First-in, first-out queues process messages in arrival order within their ordering rules. That alone does not guarantee the order of every action across your app.
values: Choose standard or first-in, first-out queues
Set request rate and simultaneous-task limits
Set message groups and capacity level
Set simultaneous-task limits; order is not guaranteed
Set task queues and worker capacity

responsibilities.label: Recovering failed tasks
responsibilities.explanation: Decide how to inspect failed work, alert someone and safely try it again. A dead-letter queue stores messages that could not be processed. Having that queue or a dashboard does not prove that retrying the work is safe.
values: Inspect task runs and retry safely
Inspect task runs and retry safely
Log and track tasks that used all retries
Handle failed messages and failure notifications
Inspect progress, reset tasks and repair failures
